target_customer: Finance teams (treasury, FP&A, accounting, internal audit) at startups and Fortune 500 companies
problem: Finance work is spread across spreadsheets and systems; traditional software is either rigid automation or manual. Concourse builds governed AI agents that trace outputs to source data.
business_model: B2B SaaS, self-serve plans for small companies and high-touch enterprise

founders.name: Matthieu Hafemeister
founders.background_notes: From YC page; AlleyWatch says both founders helped scale Jeeves to a $2.1B unicorn.

founders.name: Ted Michaels
founders.background_notes: Described in a search summary as Jeeves' former head of finance; YC page gives no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents must connect to ERPs and data warehouses, compute in code for accuracy and provide audit trails; reliability with LLMs in finance was hard in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations and encoded business logic lock in enterprise customers, but horizontal AI and ERP vendors can offer similar agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Concourse found; Concourse itself acquired Cambrean around early 2026 per AlleyWatch.

market_need_then: Finance teams were spreadsheet heavy and the founders saw the gap at Jeeves; LLMs made flexible automation newly possible in 2023.

branding.domain_note: Company site is concourse.ai; a profile site lists concourse.co. History not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct, focused on control and auditability

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch coverage at the 2024 launch; no evidence of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning and credible press but the name is a common word shared with other products; no brand level community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Concourse reported a Series A of $12M in January 2026 led by Standard Capital with a16z and CRV, after a seed in October 2024, and says it serves 100+ finance departments including Fortune 500 firms. Founders came from Jeeves and match the finance problem. It acquired Cambrean and moved to a hybrid self-serve and enterprise model.
notes: A seed amount of $4.7M appears only on Seedtable (aggregator), so the seed amount is null. AlleyWatch states $27M total raised, while other aggregators list totals from $9.4M to $27M. Series A date is January 27, 2026 per the press release in search results; recorded as 2026-01. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found (Mosaic and Datarails appear only in 2024 plus results), so the list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown or layoffs; other Concord hits concern a game studio.
